Subject: Post-call: Logging & Redaction Requirements (PII, retention, headers)

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on logging and data handling, plus next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we covered:
- You primarily need request/response logging for debugging and metrics, but logs cannot contain raw PII (card numbers, SSNs, full emails) by default.
- Retention window target: 90 days for request/response payloads, 1 year for audit metadata.
- Concern about headers / trace IDs potentially leaking user identifiers — want clear guidance on what we store and how we mask.
- Need ability to opt-out of storing request/response payloads entirely for regulated customer subsets.

Agreed next steps: 
1) I’ll send our standard logging controls doc and a short matrix of what we capture by default vs. what can be turned off or redacted. (Rishi / Neha looping in for technical specifics.)
2) Alex / Sec team to confirm retention windows and any special data residency needs (if EU region required).
3) If that looks good, we can propose a scoped PoC (30 days) with logging-in-no-plaintext mode and a small trial quota.

Attachments: I’ve attached the controls summary and a retention matrix for quick review.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the summary. Couple of clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) Can you confirm whether trace IDs or correlation IDs are ever derived from customer identifiers? If so, can those be salted or rolled?
2) For request headers, we need an explicit list of headers you store by default and which headers are redacted — e.g., Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Id.
3) If we request payload redaction, is that applied before logs hit storage (server-side) or is it a post-processing job? We need guarantees that raw payloads won’t be present even transiently for regulated flows.

Also: we may need logs stored in us-east-1 only. Is regional residency configurable per account?

Thanks —

Hi Alex —

Great questions — answered inline below. Looping Rishi and Neha for the technical confirmation and to attach the detailed controls doc.

1) Trace IDs: We do not derive trace IDs from customer identifiers. IDs are random 128-bit values generated at the runtime hop. For customers that require additional protection we can:
   - Salt and rotate correlation keys on a configurable cadence, or
   - Allow you to supply your own correlation IDs which we will hash-before-storage.

2) Headers: By default our logging includes a small allowlist: Host, Content-Type, User-Agent, X-Request-Id. We redact Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, and any header matching regex /(.*pass.*|.*secret.*)/i. We can extend the redact list on a per-account basis.

3) Redaction timing: Redaction is applied at the ingestion layer before logs are written to persistent storage. For additional assurance we support a mode where raw payloads are never instantiated in host memory — redaction performed in-stream — and an audit can be provided.

Region: Yes, account-level regional residency is supported for log storage (us-east-1, eu-west-1). We’ll confirm options and any cost delta.

Rishi / Neha — can you confirm the in-stream redaction option and attach the more detailed table of what’s captured by each retention tier?

Best,
Marissa

Hey all —

Quick tech notes to confirm: 

- Trace IDs: Runtime generates cryptographically random UUID-like values. We never use customer email/ID as an input. We support server-side HMAC of provided IDs; keys rotate at customer-configured intervals.
- Headers: Default allowlist = [Host, Content-Type, User-Agent, X-Request-Id]. All auth-related headers (Authorization, Cookie) are dropped at the ingestion proxy. Additional header redaction can be configured via account policy (matches or explicit list).
- Payload redaction: We have two modes:
    1) Log-and-redact: payloads are ingested into a short-lived buffer then redacted and written. Buffer lifetime < 500ms and is ephemeral memory only (no disk).
    2) In-stream redact: redaction performed by the proxy (Lua filter) as data passes through; raw payloads are never materialized in host memory. This is what we recommend for regulated flows.
- Retention: configurable per account. Default 90 days for payloads, 365 days for metadata. We can set payload retention to 0 (do not store) while still keeping metadata for observability.

I’ve attached the detailed controls doc and a matrix showing which fields are present at each retention tier. Happy to set up a short tech call with your SecOps to walk through implementation.

Attachments: redwood-logging-controls.pdf

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
